verses.zh: 你们要称谢耶和华，因他本为善；他的慈爱永远长存！
verses.en: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good,and his loyal love endures.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 118. The psalmist thanks God for his deliverance and urges others to join him in praise.

verses.zh: 愿以色列说：他的慈爱永远长存！
verses.en: Let Israel say,“Yes, his loyal love endures.”

verses.zh: 愿亚伦的家说：他的慈爱永远长存！
verses.en: Let the family[NOTE:1] of Aaron say,“Yes, his loyal love endures.”
notes: Or “is forever.”

verses.zh: 愿敬畏耶和华的说：他的慈爱永远长存！
verses.en: Let the loyal followers of the Lord[NOTE:1] say,“Yes, his loyal love endures.”
notes: Heb “house.”

verses.zh: 我在急难中求告耶和华，他就应允我，把我安置在宽阔之地。
verses.en: In my distress[NOTE:1] I cried out to the Lord.The Lord answered me and put me in a wide open place.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fearers of the Lord.” See Ps 15:4.
Heb “from the distress.” The noun מֵצַר (metsar, “straits; distress”) occurs only here and in Lam 1:3. In Ps 116:3 מֵצַר should probably be emended to מְצָדֵי (metsade, “snares of”).

verses.zh: 有耶和华帮助我，我必不惧怕，人能把我怎么样呢？
verses.en: The Lord is on my side;[NOTE:1] I am not afraid.What can people do to me?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the Lord answered me in a wide open place.”
Heb “for me.”

verses.zh: 在那帮助我的人中，有耶和华帮助我，所以我要看见那恨我的人遭报。
verses.en: The Lord is on my side[NOTE:1] as my helper.[NOTE:2] I look in triumph on those who hate me.
notes: The rhetorical question assumes the answer, “Nothing!” The imperfect is used in a modal sense here, indicating capability or potential. See Ps 56:11.
Heb “for me.”

verses.zh: 投靠耶和华，强似倚赖人；
verses.en: It is better to take shelter[NOTE:1] in the Lordthan to trust in people.
notes: Heb “among my helpers.” The preposition may indicate identity here, while the plural may be one of majesty or respect.

verses.zh: 投靠耶和华，强似倚赖王子。
verses.en: It is better to take shelter in the Lordthan to trust in princes.

verses.zh: 万民围绕我，我靠耶和华的名必剿灭他们。
verses.en: All the nations surrounded me.[NOTE:1] Indeed, in the name of the Lord[NOTE:2] I pushed them away.[NOTE:3]
notes: “Taking shelter” in the Lord is an idiom for seeking his protection. Seeking his protection presupposes and even demonstrates the subject’s loyalty to the Lord. In the psalms those who “take shelter” in the Lord are contrasted with the wicked and equated with those who love, fear, and serve the Lord (Pss 5:11-12; 31:17-20; 34:21-22).
The reference to an attack by the nations suggests the psalmist may have been a military leader.
In this context the phrase “in the name of the Lord” means “by the Lord’s power.”

verses.zh: 他们环绕我，围困我，我靠耶和华的名必剿灭他们。
verses.en: They surrounded me, yes, they surrounded me.Indeed, in the name of the Lord I pushed them away.

verses.zh: 他们如同蜂子围绕我，好像烧荆棘的火，必被熄灭；我靠耶和华的名，必剿灭他们。
verses.en: They surrounded me like bees.But they disappeared as quickly[NOTE:1] as a fire among thorns.[NOTE:2] Indeed, in the name of the Lord I pushed them away.
notes: Traditionally the verb has been derived from מוּל (mul, “to circumcise”) and translated “[I] cut [them] off” (see BDB 557-58 s.v. II מוּל). However, it is likely that this is a homonym meaning “to fend off” (see HALOT 556 s.v. II מול) or “to push away.” In this context, where the psalmist is reporting his past experience, the prefixed verbal form is best understood as a preterite. The phrase also occurs in vv. 11, 12.
Heb “were extinguished.”

verses.zh: 你推我，要叫我跌倒，但耶和华帮助了我。
verses.en: “You aggressively attacked me[NOTE:1] and tried to knock me down,[NOTE:2] but the Lord helped me.
notes: The point seems to be that the hostility of the nations (v. 10) is short-lived, like a fire that quickly devours thorns and then burns out. Some, attempting to create a better parallel with the preceding line, emend דֹּעֲכוּ (doʿakhu, “they were extinguished”) to בָּעֲרוּ (baʿaru, “they burned”). In that case the statement emphasizes their hostility.

Heb “pushing, you pushed me.” The infinitive absolute emphasizes the following verbal idea. The psalmist appears to address the nations as if they were an individual enemy. Some find this problematic and emend the verb form (which is a Qal perfect second masculine singular with a first person singular suffix) to נִדְחֵיתִי (nidkheti), a Niphal perfect first common singular, “I was pushed.”

verses.zh: 耶和华是我的力量，是我的诗歌；他也成了我的拯救。
verses.en: The Lord gives me strength and protects me;[NOTE:1] he has become my deliverer.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to fall,” i.e., “that [I] might fall.”

Heb “my strength and protection [is] the Lord.” The Hebrew term זִמְרָת (zimrat) is traditionally understood as meaning “song” (“my strength and song [is] the Lord”) in which case one might translate, “for the Lord gives me strength and joy” (i.e., a reason to sing). However, many recent commentators have argued that the noun זִמְרָת is here a homonym, meaning “protection” or “strength.” See HALOT 274 s.v.; cf. NEB “The Lord is my refuge and defence”; NRSV “my strength and my might.”

verses.zh: 在义人的帐棚里，有欢呼拯救的声音；耶和华的右手施展大能。
verses.en: They celebrate deliverance in the tents of the godly.[NOTE:1] The Lord’s right hand conquers.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “salvation.”
Heb “the sound of a ringing shout and deliverance [is] in the tents of the godly.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的右手高举；耶和华的右手施展大能。
verses.en: The Lord’s right hand gives victory;[NOTE:1] the Lord’s right hand conquers.
notes: Heb “does valiantly.” The statement refers here to military success (see Num 24:18; 1 Sam 14:48; Pss 60:12; 108:13).

verses.zh: 我必不致死，仍要存活，并要传扬耶和华的作为。
verses.en: I will not die, but live,and I will proclaim what the Lord has done.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “exalts.”

verses.zh: 耶和华虽严严地惩治我，却未曾将我交于死亡。
verses.en: The Lord severely[NOTE:1] punished me,but he did not hand me over to death.
notes: Heb “the works of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 给我敞开义门；我要进去称谢耶和华！
verses.en: Open for me the gates of the just king’s temple.[NOTE:1] I will enter through them and give thanks to the Lord.
notes: The infinitive absolute emphasizes the following verbal idea.

verses.zh: 这是耶和华的门；义人要进去！
verses.en: This is the Lord’s gate—the godly enter through it.

verses.zh: 我要称谢你，因为你已经应允我，又成了我的拯救！
verses.en: I will give you thanks, for you answered me,and have become my deliverer.

verses.zh: 匠人所弃的石头已成了房角的头块石头。
verses.en: The stone that the builders discarded[NOTE:1] has become the cornerstone.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the gates of justice.” The gates of the Lord’s temple are referred to here, as v. 20 makes clear. They are called “gates of justice” because they are the entrance to the just king’s palace. This has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “rejected.”

verses.zh: 这是耶和华所做的，在我们眼中看为希奇。
verses.en: This is the Lord’s work.We consider it amazing![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the head of the corner.”sn The metaphor of the stone…the builders discarded describes the way in which God’s deliverance reversed the psalmist’s circumstances. When he was in distress, he was like a stone which was discarded by builders as useless, but now that he has been vindicated by God, all can see that he is of special importance to God, like the cornerstone of the building.

verses.zh: 这是耶和华所定的日子，我们在其中要高兴欢喜！
verses.en: This is the day the Lord has brought about.[NOTE:1] We will be happy and rejoice in it.
notes: Heb “it is amazing in our eyes.” The use of the plural pronoun here and in vv. 24-27 suggests that the psalmist may be speaking for the entire nation. However, it is more likely that vv. 22-27 are the people’s response to the psalmist’s thanksgiving song (see especially v. 26). They rejoice with him because his deliverance on the battlefield (see vv. 10-12) had national repercussions.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你拯救！耶和华啊，求你使我们亨通！
verses.en: Please, Lord, deliver!Please, Lord, grant us success![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “this is the day the Lord has made.” Though sometimes applied in a general way, this statement in its context refers to the day of deliverance which the psalmist and people celebrate.

verses.zh: 奉耶和华名来的是应当称颂的！我们从耶和华的殿中为你们祝福！
verses.en: May the one who comes in the name of the Lord[NOTE:1] be blessed.We will pronounce blessings on you[NOTE:2] in the Lord’s temple.[NOTE:3]
notes: A petition for deliverance and success seems odd in a psalm thanking God for deliverance, but it is not unique (see Ps 9:19-20). The people ask God to continue to intervene for them as he has for the psalmist.
The people refer here to the psalmist, who enters the Lord’s temple to thank him publicly (see vv. 19-21), as the one who comes in the name of the Lord.

The pronominal suffix is second masculine plural, but the final mem (ם) is probably dittographic (note the mem [מ] at the beginning of the following form) or enclitic, in which case the suffix may be taken as second masculine singular, referring to the psalmist.

verses.zh: 耶和华是　神；他光照了我们。理当用绳索把祭牲拴住，牵到坛角那里。
verses.en: The Lord is God, and he has delivered us.[NOTE:1] Tie the offering[NOTE:2] with ropesto the horns of the altar.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “from the house of the Lord.”

Heb “and he has given us light.” This may be an elliptical expression, with “his face” being implied as the object (see Num 6:25; Pss 31:16; 67:1; 80:3, 7, 19). In this case, “his face has given us light” = “he has smiled on us,” or “he has shown us his favor.” Another option (the one reflected in the translation) is that “light” here symbolizes divine blessing in the form of deliverance. “Light” is often used as a metaphor for deliverance and the life/blessings it brings. See Pss 37:6; 97:11; 112:4; Isa 49:6; 51:4; Mic 7:8. Some prefer to repoint the preterite form וַיָּאֶר (vayyaʾer, “he made light”) as a jussive וְיָאֵר (veyaʾer; “may he make light [for us]”).

The Hebrew noun חַג (khag) normally means “festival,” but here it apparently refers metonymically to an offering made at the festival. BDB 291 s.v. חַג 2 interprets the word in this way here, citing as comparable the use of later Hebrew חֲגִיגָה, which can refer to both a festival and a festival offering (see Jastrow 424 s.v. חֲגִיגָה).

verses.zh: 你是我的　神，我要称谢你！你是我的　神，我要尊崇你！
verses.en: You are my[NOTE:1] God, and I will give you thanks.You are my God, and I will praise you.
notes: The second half of v. 27 has been translated and interpreted in a variety of ways. For a survey of major views, see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 122.

verses.zh: 你们要称谢耶和华，因他本为善；他的慈爱永远长存！
verses.en: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is goodand his loyal love endures.[NOTE:1]
notes: You are my God. The psalmist speaks again (see v. 21), responding to the words of the worshipers (vv. 22-27).
